findings.reader: A tight, well-scoped dated news piece: it explains the September 16 upload incident causally, preserves OpenAI's not-a-frequency-estimate limit and the analyst's internal-and-voluntary caveat, and converts the incident into a portable answer-versus-action permission check grounded in a specific daily-life handoff. All reader outcomes pass and no failure family is present.
findings.facts: All material claims check out against the OpenAI disclosure and AP report: the September 16 framework and six reports, the Python-then-upload example from an unreleased model, OpenAI's explicit instruction not to read the reports as a frequency estimate, and the work-in-progress/internal-and-voluntary limits, each correctly attributed. Factual integrity, freshness, dated change, and consequence-with-uncertainty all pass.
